summary: Focus heavily on dinosaur and automobile safety topics as they consistently outperform other categories in both raw views and retention. Craft first sentences as direct, counter-intuitive assertions or relatable second-person challenges rather than academic questions. Maintain titles that directly match the core curiosity gap in the hook without over-explaining the science upfront. Avoid using mixed-script Hinglish or purely English technical titles for this audience since local-language curiosity performs better. Keep video concepts focused on tangible, physical objects that viewers encounter or can easily visualize.
winning_hooks: जो car crash में पिचक जाती है, वो तुम्हें ज़्यादा बचाती है।
सोचो, तुम्हारे दांतों पर 3 छोटी cars एक के ऊपर एक रख दी जाएं। इतने ज़ोर से T. rex काटता था।
avoid: Academic or passive scientific framing like 'डायनासोर के जीवाश्मों में वैज्ञानिकों को...' that delays the core point.
English technical titles like 'Why Your Smoke Detector Is Radioactive 😱' which result in low stayed_pct.
next_experiment: Test a dinosaur-related topic using a pure Hindi/Hinglish title combined with a second-person conversational hook ('सोचो अगर तुम...') to verify if it replicates the high stayed_pct of the top car and T. rex videos.
